# `supabase/service-role-in-client`: Supabase service_role key used in client-side code

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:rules` from the rule metadata in src/rules/. Edit only the
     hand:* regions here; everything else comes from the rule and is overwritten. -->

| Family   | Default severity | GitHub security-severity | CWE                                                                                                                                                                                |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| supabase | critical         | 9.5                      | [CWE-269](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/269.html), [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html), [CWE-522](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/522.html) |

Individual findings can have a lower or higher severity than the default, and each has a
confidence (high, medium or low). Both are explained below.

## What it detects

<!-- hand:detects -->

The Supabase service-role key reaching browser code:

- the service-role environment variable (`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` and similar names)
  referenced in a module classified as client-side;
- a client-side module importing a local module that uses the service-role key.

A module is client-side when it has `'use client'` or `import 'client-only'`, is a Pages
Router page, or lives in a Vite / Create React App `src/` (Expo `app/`) tree. Hardcoded
service-role JWTs and `sb_secret_` keys anywhere are reported by
[`secrets/provider-key`](../secrets/provider-key.md).

<!-- /hand:detects -->

## Why it matters

The service_role (or sb_secret_) key bypasses Row Level Security entirely. Code that runs in the browser either ships that key to every visitor, or (when the bundler strips a non-public env var) silently breaks and invites the "fix" of making it public. Client components must only ever use the anon/publishable key.

## Messages

What a finding from this rule says (parameters in braces):

- {name} (service-role key) is referenced in client-side code ({reason}).
- Client-side code ({reason}) imports {module}, which uses the service-role key.

## How to fix

Move privileged operations to server code (route handler, server action, edge function) that authenticates the user first. In client code, use the anon key and let RLS policies decide. Mark admin modules with import 'server-only' so the build fails if a client component imports them.

### Vulnerable

```ts
'use client';
import { supabaseAdmin } from '@/lib/supabase/admin'; // service_role client
export function DeleteUser({ id }: { id: string }) {
  return <button onClick={() => supabaseAdmin.auth.admin.deleteUser(id)}>Delete</button>;
}
```

### Fixed

```ts
// lib/supabase/admin.ts
import 'server-only';
// ...

// app/admin/actions.ts
('use server');
export async function deleteUser(id: string) {
  const user = await requireAdmin(); // authenticate + authorise first
  await supabaseAdmin().auth.admin.deleteUser(id);
}
```

## False positives and limitations

<!-- hand:false-positives -->

- **Unknown modules are not reported.** Without a full import graph, shared modules
  (`lib/`, `utils/`) are "unknown" and the rule stays silent. That avoids false positives
  but misses keys that reach the browser through a shared module.
- **Server code in a client-looking location** (a script in a Vite `src/` tree that only
  runs in Node): mark it with `import 'server-only'`, move it, or suppress with the reason.
- **Mitigation that is not a fix:** a bundler that strips non-public env vars makes the key
  `undefined` in the browser instead of leaking it. The finding is still reported, because
  the code is broken and the usual "fix" is adding a public prefix.

<!-- /hand:false-positives -->

## How to suppress

Only suppress a finding after confirming it is safe. Put the directive on the line above
the reported line (or use `vibeguard-ignore-line` on the line itself, or
`vibeguard-ignore-file` anywhere in the file). The reason is required: a directive without
one suppresses nothing and is reported.

```ts
// vibeguard-ignore-next-line supabase/service-role-in-client -- explain why this is safe (at least 10 characters)
<the line VibeGuard reported>
```

Use the comment syntax of the file: `//` or `/* */` in code, `#` in `.env` and YAML
files, `--` in SQL.

To turn the rule off or change its severity for the whole project, use `.vibeguard.yml`:

```yaml
version: 1
rules:
  supabase/service-role-in-client: off # or: { severity: low }
```

See [configuration](../../configuration.md) and
[ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-suppression-design.md).

## CWE

- [CWE-269](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/269.html): Improper Privilege Management
- [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html): Improper Access Control
- [CWE-522](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/522.html): Insufficiently Protected Credentials
